learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the principles of modern operating systems.
System programming and concurrent programming capabilities.

syllabus_topics: Process management in UNIX / Linux: states, representation, management (scheduling), operations and commands related to processes
Scheduling algorithms: FCFS, SJF, with priority, round-robin, with multiple queues.
Scheduling in UNIX, Linux and WinXP
Interaction between processes by message passing:
direct / indirect, symmetrical / asymmetrical communication, buffering
interaction between Unix processes: pipe and fifo, synchronization through signals
the UNIX file system: logical and physical organization, commands and system calls for managing and accessing files / directories
contiguous memory allocation: single partition and multiple partitions; fragmentation;
memory memory management in UNIX / Linux
The problem of mutual exclusion and its solutions.
synchronization tools in the shared memory model: the semaphore
Management of devices: program control, interruption-based and DMA.
teaching_methods: Individual concurrent programming practice in laboratory

assessment_methods.method: Practical examination (in Lab) consisting in the development of concurrent programs in GNU/Linux and Java environments

assessment_rules: The final evaluation will take into account the results of a written theory test on the concepts taught, a practical examination in the lab, and an optional oral examination.
bibliography: P. Ancilotti, M. Boari, A. Ciampolini, G. Lipari: Sistemi Operativi, seconda edizione, McGraw-Hill, 2008.
institution: Università Di Bologna - Alma Mater Studiorum — Ingegneria informatica
